headline: Democrats sweep Congress, oil slides, and Nifty eyes a gap-up start

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning, and welcome to your Market Brief for Thursday, the fifth of November.

Three things matter most today. First, the Democrats have won control of both houses of the US Congress. Wall Street loved it, the dollar slipped, and oil fell sharply on hopes that the war with Iran could end sooner.

Second, that oil slide is good news for India. Brent crude is now around 94 dollars a barrel, its fourth day of falls. GIFT Nifty is pointing to a strong, gap-up start, after the Nifty's longest winning streak since June.

And third, it's a heavy results day. Titan, Bharti Airtel, Mahindra and Mahindra, LIC, ONGC and Britannia all report today.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Now to how markets closed on Wednesday. The Sensex gained about 384 points to end at 77,301. The Nifty closed at 23,961. Both are at two-month highs. The Nifty has now risen for five straight sessions, gaining about five and a half percent in that time.

Media, metals and realty led the way, and consumer goods did well too. Information technology shares fell, weighed down by worries around artificial intelligence.

The money flows tell an interesting story. Foreign institutional investors bought shares worth 7,284 crore rupees, their fourth straight day of buying. Domestic institutional investors sold about 3,712 crore rupees, also for a fourth day.

In the bond market, the ten-year government bond yield fell nearly 11 basis points, its sharpest drop in seven months. The rupee gained for a fourth session as oil fell.

This morning, GIFT Nifty is trading near 24,300, up around 350 points. For levels, analysts quoted by Moneycontrol see 24,200 as the first target, with 24,350 to 24,400 as strong resistance. Ajit Mishra of Religare sees room towards 24,400 to 24,700. But some technical analysts told Business Standard that only a move above 24,780 would signal the broader trend is improving.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
On to the primary market. BLS Polymers had a stellar debut, listing at a 65 percent premium after its issue was subscribed 241 times. The shares rose almost 6 percent more on Wednesday.

The market regulator, the Securities and Exchange Board of India, has cleared three more companies to launch public issues: Mahanadi Coalfields, Sagar Defence Engineering and Arjun Jewellers. Sebi has also set up a working group to revive its Innovators Growth Platform, the listing route for start-ups that has seen little use since 2014. It wants to make it easier for deep-tech, biotech and space companies to raise money.

And in deals, Nykaa says it will buy an 82 percent stake in Simply Nam.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
Now to the results, starting with the new-age consumer names. Lenskart's profit more than doubled, up 122 percent to 227 crore rupees, as revenue grew about 36 percent to 2,845 crore. It added 165 stores in the quarter. Nykaa's profit tripled to 101 crore rupees, with revenue up 28 percent to about 3,006 crore.

In financials, BSE's profit jumped 45 percent to 809 crore rupees, with revenue up 34 percent. Its board also accepted an offer for a plot in Mumbai's Bandra Kurla Complex. In the State Bank group, SBI's profit grew about 14 percent and SBI Cards' jumped 75 percent. Analysts said SBI Cards beat estimates, SBI was in line, and SBI Life, up 11 percent, missed. Bajaj Finserv's revenue rose 17 percent to 43,416 crore rupees.

In healthcare, it was a mixed picture. Zydus Lifesciences saw profit fall about 27 percent to 925 crore rupees, even as revenue rose 29 percent, because costs climbed sharply. Dr Lal PathLabs did better, with profit up 27 percent to 192 crore, as it tested about 14 percent more samples.

A few more. Saregama's profit rose 46 percent to 64 crore rupees, and the shares jumped 13 percent. Awfis Space Solutions saw profit up 94 percent. Bayer CropScience grew profit 9 percent to 166 crore despite a 19 percent fall in revenue, blaming an erratic monsoon, and declared an interim dividend of 90 rupees a share.

Today's big one is Titan. Brokerages expect its profit to rise by up to 27 percent, with jewellery growth and margins in focus.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
Turning to the economy. India's services sector grew at its fastest pace in four months in October. The HSBC services purchasing managers' index rose to 55.8, from 55.2 in September, on strong domestic demand. Input cost inflation was the lowest in more than six years, though hiring slowed. Factory growth eased a little, to 54.7, but export orders grew at their fastest pace in six months.

Tax collections are strong. Goods and services tax collections for October rose 23 percent to 2.3 lakh crore rupees, the fastest growth in over four years, helped by a 42 percent jump in revenue from imports.

The rupee has gained about 1.25 percent since October, after the Reserve Bank curbed speculative bets. But it is still down over 5 percent against the dollar this year. The Reserve Bank has also set up a technical committee with banks and market players to review how money markets are working.

On the other side, the farm picture is worrying. Rabi sowing is down 46 percent from last year, to 37.6 lakh hectares, after a 48 percent rainfall shortfall in October. Retail sugar prices have climbed over 4 rupees a kilo in a month, to about 59 rupees fifty paise.

And Budget wish lists are coming in. The industry body FICCI wants long-term capital gains tax on listed shares removed, paid for by a higher securities transaction tax. SBI Research has proposed no such tax after three years of holding. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said she will consider investors' concerns on equity taxation.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Around the world, the US midterms dominated. The Democrats won both houses of Congress, in what reports called a rebuke of President Trump over the Iran war and inflation.

Wall Street rallied hard. The Dow jumped about 1,570 points, or 3 percent. The S&P 500 rose 1.6 percent, and the Nasdaq 1.4 percent. Amazon surged over 7 percent. But data centre stocks fell, on fears of tighter rules on artificial intelligence. Treasury yields dropped and the dollar had its weakest day in two months.

In Asia, that same fear hit chipmakers. Samsung and SK Hynix fell more than 5 percent each, dragging South Korea's Kospi down over 3 percent. Japanese carmakers like Toyota and Honda rose about 5 percent.

Oil is the big one for us. Brent crude has slid for a fourth day, to around 94 dollars a barrel, on hopes a Democratic Congress could push for an end to the war with Iran. Gold climbed about 3 percent, back above 4,000 dollars an ounce.

One item close to home. The United States has sanctioned an India-based couple and several linked companies, accusing them of helping Iran's shadow fleet of oil tankers with fraudulent ship registrations.

segments.script: An update on the India–US trade deal you're following. With the Democrats now in charge of Congress, Indian officials are said to be cautiously optimistic, seeing some relief on trade tension, but new uncertainty too. The Global Trade Research Initiative warns that President Trump may now press India harder for a quick deal on American terms.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Finally, your money. If you have family abroad, this one is for them. From the third of December, Sebi will let non-resident Indians, Overseas Citizens of India and foreign nationals in compliant countries complete their investor KYC digitally, without being physically present in India. Video verification will be allowed where needed.

Sebi has also recommended that switching from one mutual fund scheme to another should not be treated as a taxable sale, if the units have been held for more than a year. That's a proposal for now, not a rule.

An investor warning. Several users of the global investing platforms Stockal and Borderless say their American shares were sold without permission, with one claiming a loss of around a million dollars. Complaints have been filed with the police and Sebi. Stockal's parent says it found no breach of its systems.

For tax watchers, the Pune bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal deleted a 60 lakh rupee addition against a widow, accepting that the cash was a gift from her late husband for her and their daughters.

With Dhanteras around the corner, two gold notes. Jewellers say the recent price correction should lift sentiment, though volumes may stay flat. And dealers are worried about a new adulteration trick using heavy metals that can fool acid and touchstone tests, so check for hallmarking and read your bill carefully.

Two more dates for your calendar. New motor insurance rules start on the fifteenth of December, with four clearly defined cover options. And after the Reserve Bank's quarter-point repo rate hike, banks are raising deposit rates, with Suryoday Small Finance Bank offering up to 8.6 percent.

That's your brief. Today, watch for a strong open and whether the Nifty can hold above 24,000, the direction of crude oil, and results from Titan, Bharti Airtel and LIC. Have a lovely Thursday, and a happy festive week.
